title: Near-lossless undirected constant-degree vertex expanders
formal: For every rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), do there exist an integer \(D\ge3\), constants \(\eta\in(0,1)\), \(a,b,C>0\), an integer \(k\ge1\), and one deterministic graph-construction algorithm \(A_\varepsilon\), such that for every integer \(m\ge1\) the algorithm outputs an undirected \(D\)-regular graph \(G_m\) with \(N_m\) vertices, takes at most \(C(m+1)^k\) bit steps, and satisfies \[a m\le N_m\le b m,\qquad |N_{G_m}(S)|\ge(1-\varepsilon)D|S|\quad\text{for every }S\subseteq V(G_m)\text{ with }|S|\le\eta N_m?\] Here explicit construction means deterministic polynomial-time output of the entire graph. All constants and the program may depend on \(\varepsilon\), but must be independent of \(m\) and \(S\).
why: Lossless vertex expansion means that nearly all incidences from a small set lead to distinct neighbors. Deterministic constant-degree families with this property supply a strong combinatorial resource for coding and network applications. Requiring an undirected graph makes the guarantee simultaneous across the whole vertex set.
status_note: Resolved for the explicitly recorded deterministic polynomial-time whole-graph construction interpretation by Hsieh–Lubotzky–Mohanty–Reiner–Zhang, FOCS 2025, Theorems 1 and 2.2. The source’s stronger fully explicit local-neighbor notion is distinguished and is not certified by this disposition. Complete statement, interpretation, provenance and reviewed proof locators are preserved in the archive.

sentences: The historical target is a deterministic construction of constant-degree undirected graphs with near-lossless vertex expansion.
Every sufficiently small vertex set must have almost the degree times its size in distinct neighbors.
The degree and the permitted small-set fraction may depend on the requested loss but remain fixed across the family.
The card fixes polynomial-time construction of the complete graph and distinguishes the stronger requirement of fast individual-neighbor computation.
A FOCS 2025 construction meets this ordinary explicitness target, so the complete reviewed record is archived as resolved.

definitions: An undirected graph here is a finite undirected multigraph, matching the source’s graph convention. Its vertex set is \(\{1,\ldots,N_m\}\). Each edge is an unordered pair of endpoints; parallel copies and loops are allowed. Degree counts one incidence at each endpoint of a nonloop edge and two incidences for a loop, and every vertex must have degree exactly \(D\). The neighborhood \(N_G(S)=\{v:\exists u\in S\text{ with an edge joining }u\text{ and }v\}\) counts distinct vertices, ignoring edge multiplicity. It may contain vertices of \(S\); it is not the external boundary \(N_G(S)\setminus S\). The guarantee concerns every set of at most the fixed positive fraction \(\eta\) of all vertices, including sets meeting both sides if the graph is bipartite. It is not just expansion from one designated side. An empty set satisfies the condition automatically. The lower bound \(D\ge3\) and the small-error range exclude the trivial degree-one matching phenomenon; the target concerns arbitrarily small losses at a nontrivial expansion factor. It suffices to quantify over rational \(\varepsilon\), since a construction with a smaller rational loss also meets any larger real loss. The input to \(A_\varepsilon\) is \(m\) in binary; its running time is polynomial in the requested graph-size parameter \(m\), not in the input’s logarithmic bit length. The output explicitly encodes \(N_m\) and a complete edge list, including multiplicities, using binary vertex identifiers and fixed delimiters. The bounds \(a m\le N_m\le b m\) permit nearby admissible sizes while guaranteeing an infinite family of unbounded, regularly available sizes. The machine is one fixed finite Turing program for each fixed \(\varepsilon\), with ordinary bit costs, no random bits, advice depending on \(m\), or oracle. Its initialization and all output writes are charged. No efficiency bound in \(1/\varepsilon\) is required. There is no additional demand for computing an individual neighbor in time polynomial in \(\log N_m\) without first constructing the graph.
answer_criterion: The historical benchmark requires a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the existence assertion or its negation. A positive answer must specify the deterministic constructors and prove their costs, degrees, size bounds and the neighborhood inequality for every allowed set and size, with the stated parameter dependence. A negative answer would have to establish failure at some fixed positive rational loss for every such choice of degree, constants and constructor. Random graph existence without deterministic polynomial construction, expansion from only one bipartite side, or expansion limited to a sublinear power of the graph size does not meet the target. The published positive result resolves the ordinary whole-graph construction formulation recorded here; it is not a claim of a Lean formalization or of the stronger local-neighbor construction guarantee.

context_blocks.text: Vadhan’s Open Problem 4.44 asks for explicit undirected vertex expanders whose small-set expansion approaches the degree. Section 4.1 defines the neighborhood without deleting the original set. Section 4.3 separately distinguishes polynomial-time whole-graph construction, called mildly explicit there, from the stronger local-neighbor notion called fully explicit. This reviewed historical card fixes the ordinary whole-graph meaning of the unqualified construction request; it does not identify the two notions or claim that the stronger one follows.

Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner and Zhang give the required deterministic polynomial-time construction in their FOCS 2025 paper. Theorem 1 gives constant-degree lossless expanders, while Theorem 2.2 supplies an explicit size-indexed family and simultaneous expansion on both sides of balanced bipartite graphs. These guarantees cover general small vertex subsets in the corresponding undirected graph.

The result allows the degree and the maximum expanded fraction to depend on the requested loss, while both stay constant throughout a graph family. It resolves the ordinary polynomial-time construction target. Questions about a smaller additive loss independent of degree or stronger local access are distinct from that target.
